g.text: HC-SR04 - the exchange, and the conversion that is the act
STATUS: RED; the conversion is EXACT on the one measurement that ran (1160 us -> 199 mm)
a burst it did not send
THE ANSWER IS THE WIDTH,\brather than a level.
WHY THE TRIGGER IS 601 CLOCKS AND NOT 600 IS WORTH
NAMING EVEN THOUGH IT IS NOT THE FAULT.
The device asks for 10 us MINIMUM, so the extra clock is harmless to a real
sensor. The check is an EQUALITY anyway, because the act claims the COUNT and
not a datasheet floor - and that is the same discipline the WS2812 act uses when
a 74-clock cell clears every window in print.
601 against 600 is a ONE-INSTRUCTION error, and a one-instruction error of
exactly this shape is what this family has found six times. It is named here as
the most likely place to look for the lost second measurement; it is NOT claimed
to be the cause, because the five failing checks do not say so.
WHY THE ECHO IS CAPTURED AND NOT SAMPLED,
what makes this act safe at 4 m.
A receiver that samples the level and decides "there is
something there" has to poll, and a poll loop that is
long relative to the distance reading adds its own
uncertainty to every sample. A receiver that measures
the WIDTH does not care when it looked: the two edges
define the interval, and the interval is the answer.
The same reason the counter is RESET at the rising edge
and READ at the falling edge rather than subtracted:
no 16-bit subtract, and this machine has no carry flag,
so a subtract is a four-case analysis on bit 7 and a
compare is the same analysis again.
THE IDENTITY, and why it removes the multiply the plan
So the conversion is a multiply by
eleven of a ten-bit number, a multiply by eleven of a six-bit number, and one
add. The plan for this act assumed a 16x16 multiply; this identity removes it,
along with the division and the approximation the plan expected the division to
A MULTIPLY BY ELEVEN IS FOUR DOUBLINGS AND TWO ADDS:
x -> 2x -> 4x -> 5x -> 10x -> 11x. No loop, no counter, no
second temporary - the multiplicand stays in Q throughout.
the second term is 11 * 63 = 693. Recorded rather than assumed, because an
unnoticed overflow in the high byte is invisible from the outside - the answer
would still be a plausible millimetre figure.
11/64 IS +0.22 % LONG AGAINST THE SPEED OF SOUND, AND THAT
The arithmetic below is EXACT for 11/64, which is a different and checkable
claim from "the range is right to two parts in a thousand". Only the first can be
asserted as an equality, and the testbench asserts the first: "us*11/64 is exact
and this is an equality". A page that reported the accuracy of the ranging would
be reporting a property of a constant that was chosen to divide, not of the
|= measurement |= echo | expected | firmware banked | result | status |=
FAIL - the second measurement never ran
Why the two targets are 1 160 us and 5 816 us.
twelve bits and the large one does not, so the pair exercises the ten-bit path
the high byte. A single target at the near end would prove the
conversion works and say nothing about the case that could overflow - and an
overflow in the high byte is invisible from the outside, because the answer would
still be a plausible millimetre figure.
